title: Base-change map
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative ring, and let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X&\xleftarrow{h}&Y\\
f\downarrow&&\downarrow e\\
S&\xleftarrow{g}&T
\end{array}
\qquad Y\cong X\times_S T,
$$
be a base-change square [sbc-def-base-change-square], with $f\circ h=g\circ e$. Use the small skeletons and derived-category universe of [def-weil-size-convention]. Work with the fixed constant coefficient ring $\Lambda$ on the small etale sites and the module derived categories $D(-_{\Et},\Lambda)$ of [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For an edge $u:U\to V$, the sheaf functors are $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ of [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image] and [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. With these constant coefficients, module pullback $u^*$ is canonically $u^{-1}$ and is exact [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Its derived functor $Lu^*$ is consequently the termwise inverse image [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. On all of $D(U_{\Et},\Lambda)$, write $Ru_*K=Q(u_*I)$ for the total right derived direct image, with $K\xrightarrow{\sim}QI$ a K-injective resolution [def-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions], [prop-weil-pbc-kinjective-resolutions-exist], [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-total-derived]. Here $Q$ is the localization from complexes to the derived category. Its restriction to $D^+$ is the derived direct image of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image]. The derived adjunction $Lu^*\dashv Ru_*$ is the canonical adjunction of [lem-pc-derived-adjoint-functors].

For $K\in D(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$, the *derived base-change map* is the
morphism

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}_{f,g}(K):Lf^*Rg_*K
\longrightarrow Rh_*Le^*K
$$

of $D(X_{\Et},\Lambda)$ defined as the composite

$$
\begin{array}{l}
Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\;\eta_e\;}
Lf^*Rg_*Re_*Le^*K
\;\cong\;Lf^*R(ge)_*Le^*K
\;\cong\;Lf^*Rf_*Rh_*Le^*K\\
\hphantom{Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\;\eta_e\;}}
\xrightarrow{\;\varepsilon_f\;}
Rh_*Le^*K,
\end{array}
$$

where $\eta_e$ is the unit of the adjunction
$Le^*\dashv Re_*$, where $ge=fh$ gives the two canonical
identifications of the composite functors [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition], these canonical identifications are normalized as the conjugates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate] of the inverse-image composition identifications, using the composite adjunctions [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction], and where
$\varepsilon_f$ is the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$; it is
the unbounded derived exchange morphism [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] on the square with the vertical and horizontal sides exchanged. Equivalently it is the inverse mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], under $Le^*\dashv Re_*$ and $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$, of the canonical direct-image square isomorphism $Rg_*Re_*\cong Rf_*Rh_*$. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$, its restriction to $D^+$ is the exchange morphism of [def-weil-pbc-derived-exchange] read on that same exchanged square. For general $\Lambda$, the bounded-below restriction uses the same mate formula in the module categories, with the exact inverse images and derived adjunctions specified above. In the inverse-image form its transpose under $Lh^*\dashv Rh_*$ is
$$
Lh^*Lf^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}}
Le^*Lg^*Rg_*K\xrightarrow{Le^*\varepsilon_g}Le^*K,
$$
where $\theta^D_{\square,\mathrm{unb}}$ is constructed in the module categories by applying the canonical inverse-image square isomorphism $h^{-1}f^{-1}\cong e^{-1}g^{-1}$ termwise. Its components commute with the differentials by naturality. Exactness of these inverse images [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact] makes their termwise composites preserve quasi-isomorphisms; clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property] therefore descends this isomorphism uniquely along $Q$, using the termwise comparison isomorphisms of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-functor]. For $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ this is precisely the unbounded square isomorphism of [def-weil-pbc-derived-square-iso]. Its
naturality in $K$ is the corresponding statement below, and its
compatibility with the composition of squares and with base change
along the square is stated separately in sbc-lem-base-change-composition and sbc-lem-identity-and-base-change-composition (pointers, not ingredients of this definition).
Specialize to $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$. For $F\in\Ab(T_{\Et})$ and $q\in\mathbf Z$, the *base-change map in degree $q$* is
the $q$-th cohomology sheaf of $\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}$ applied to
$F$ (placed in degree zero):

$$
{\operatorname{BC}}^q_{f,g}(F):=H^q\bigl(\operatorname{BC}_{f,g}(F)\bigr)
:f^{-1}R^qg_*F
\longrightarrow R^qh_*e^{-1}F,
$$

the identifications of the two sides following from exactness of
$f^{-1}$ and of $e^{-1}$ (take $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$ in [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]) and the natural comparison $H^q(u^{-1}C)\cong u^{-1}H^q(C)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], together with the definitions of the
higher direct images of
[def-weil-pbc-direct-image]; in degree $q=0$ this is the
sheaf-level base-change map obtained by the composition

$$
h^{-1}f^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{\theta_\square}
e^{-1}g^{-1}g_*F\xrightarrow{e^{-1}\varepsilon_g}e^{-1}F
$$

(valid for $q=0$ because the counit
$\varepsilon_g:g^{-1}g_*\to\operatorname{id}$ is a morphism of
functors on sheaves on $T_{\Et}$), transposed under
$h^{-1}\dashv h_*$.
The identification with the usual degreewise base-change map, including the displayed degree-zero transpose of the underived exchange [def-weil-pbc-underived-exchange], is [lem-kun-bc-map-on-cohomology] on the exchanged square. For module sheaves the same definition uses $F\in\Mod(T_{\Et},\Lambda)$; the abelian-sheaf clause is the specialization $\Lambda=\mathbf Z$.

proof.text: Keep the set-valued unit/composition/counit construction. For abelian complexes form the termwise inverse-image square comparison and take its mate along the unbounded inverse-image/right-derived-direct-image adjunctions. Iterating mates identifies its direct-image mate with the composite of rightDerivedLowerStarComp, rightDerivedLowerStarCongr and the inverse composition comparison, because these comparisons are adjunction conjugates. The inverse-mate component formula therefore gives exactly the previously specified unit/direct-image-comparison/counit arrow. This equivalent presentation avoids expensive definitional comparison of generated derived-adjunction instance proofs. The equality with the original formula is proved in the private abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow_eq_pushforward_formula helper of AbelianDerivedExchangePlusCompatibility. Repair after the A4 landing: keep the public abelianDerivedBaseChangeTransformation signature and define it by this mate; keep abelianDerivedBaseChangeArrow exactly its component. The private abelianDerivedBaseChangeTransformation_eq_pushforward theorem identifies the mate with the entire natural-transformation composite landed by A4, so its naturality interface is preserved.

proof_origin.place: Same canonical exchange construction, using iterated mates and conjugate composition comparisons; B2 equivalent definitional presentation, verified by a Lean equality with the original formula.

lean.note: Interface repair under brief-stage2 §1(B): the recorded derivedBaseChangeMap requires monoidal coefficients; it does not specialize directly to AddCommGrpCat, and supplies no set-valued exchange. The original module-coefficient map is retained by importing its original module, not redefined. This module adds the canonical set exchange, its standard inverse-image adjunction, and the unbounded abelian exchange using exact termwise inverse image and total right derived direct image. Both arrows use the unit-e/composition/counit-f formula of the node, with canonical (conjugate-normalized in the derived case) direct-image composition comparisons. No arbitrary map, coefficient restriction, or boundedness assumption is introduced. Stage-3 A4: factor the same abelian unit/comparison/counit construction through a natural transformation, then evaluate its component. Unit, composition comparisons, counit and directions are unchanged. This supplies naturality without unfolding derived functors. See coord/changes/A4-abelian-exchange-natural-transformation.md; the definition change reopens review for dependent targets.
